title: Quantized Transport through a Supermoiré Chern Mosaic
authors: Li-Qiao Xia, Aviram Uri, Zachary W. Gomez, Molly P. Andersen, Julian May-Mann, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Trithep Devakul, Yves H. Kwan, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Aaron Sharpe
abstract: Magic-angle helical trilayer graphene---three graphene layers sequentially twisted in the same direction by $\sim1.8^\circ$---relaxes into a mosaic of domains that, at zero field, carry opposite valley-resolved Chern numbers, with boundaries hosting a network of gapless conducting modes. Charge transport through this network depends sensitively on how the modes connect and scatter, making well-quantized transport unlikely. Contrary to this expectation, we observe a field-induced Chern gap with Chern number $C=-6$ emanating from charge neutrality; in this gap, the Hall resistance is quantized to within $2\%$ of the expected value, $-h/6e^2$, at 4.6 K. We explain this behavior using both Hofstadter and orbital Zeeman calculations, which show that a moderate magnetic field drives a valley-selective topological transition. Above the transition, the total Chern number of the occupied states in each spin-valley flavor becomes identical across neighboring domains, and the domain-wall modes can become gapped. Though the central valence-band Chern numbers still differ between the two domain types, the observed quantized transport attests to a global gap.
summary: This work reports the observation of quantized Hall resistance in a supermoiré Chern mosaic formed from twisted graphene, contradicting initial expectations of gapless transport. The authors explain this robust quantization by proposing that a moderate magnetic field drives a valley-selective topological transition, establishing a global Chern insulator state with a Chern number of -6.
main_problem: The study investigates the mechanism behind quantized charge transport in a Supermoiré Chern Mosaic, contrasting the expected unquantized behavior from domain-wall modes with the observed quantized Hall resistance.
main_result: The system exhibits a robust, quantized Hall resistance ($R_{yx} \approx -h/6e^2$) under a perpendicular magnetic field, attributed to a field-induced, valley-selective topological transition that gaps the domain-wall modes.
method: The research combines magnetotransport measurements (Landau fan measurements) with theoretical calculations using the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model and the Hofstadter spectrum analysis.
model_or_system: The physical system is helical trilayer graphene (HTG) twisted by a magic angle ($\sim 1.8^\circ$), forming a supermoiré mosaic of domains with opposite valley-resolved Chern numbers.
key_observables: Quantized Hall resistance ($R_{yx}$), longitudinal resistance ($R_{xx}$), and the topological invariant, the Chern number ($C$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (e.g., 4.6 K), perpendicular magnetic field ($B$), and the twist angle ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the orbital Zeeman model and assumes that the observed quantization implies a global gap, overriding the expected gapless domain-wall transport.
figures_summary: Figures show magnetotransport data (Landau Fans) confirming quantized plateaus, and theoretical figures illustrate the evolution of the Hofstadter spectrum and the conditions for a global Chern gap.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical system and the initial theoretical conflict (gapless vs. quantized transport) to presenting experimental measurements confirming quantization, and finally developing theoretical models (Hofstadter/Orbital Zeeman) to explain the field-induced topological transition responsible for the global gap.
why_interesting: The mechanism of field-induced topological phase transitions in moiré heterostructures, which can be modeled using continuum theories and analyzed via Chern numbers, provides a rich platform for understanding emergent topological quantum phenomena relevant to quantum simulation.
